plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with three bidders. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit, independent of others’ strategies or history. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above risks negative profit if I win and pay above my value. With 0.1 bid increments and no useful history in a single round, I will bid exactly my value. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. There’s no prior history to exploit this round. Overbidding risks winning and paying above my value if the second-highest bid lies between my value and my inflated bid. Underbidding risks losing when I would have profited. With $0.1 bid increments, bidding exactly my value ($46) maximizes expected profit. Ties are random; no gain from shading. Therefore, bid 46. ]

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is truthful bidding: bid your exact value. This maximizes expected profit and avoids losing when winning would be profitable. With value $35, I will bid 35. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, yielding profit 35 minus that bid; if I lose, profit is 0. There is no benefit to shading in this format, even with three bidders and random tie-breaking.
